correctness.rationale: The piecewise-linear interpolant has L2 norm at most sqrt(L) times the sample l2 norm and derivative norm at most 2/sqrt(delta) times that norm. Poincare-Wirtinger gives the stated one-sequence inequality, including the regularity upgrade when only the derivative and samples are initially known to be square-integrable. Applying it first to the continuous reciprocal transform yields t psi in L2; applying it to the ordinary transform and combining the two inequalities gives both displayed estimates with the factor 1-alpha beta. The unitary Fourier normalization and both reciprocal norm identities were checked explicitly.

value.rationale: Exact uniqueness does not quantify the effect of noisy Fourier observations. The estimate gives a finite, explicit density-norm bound in terms of square-summable residuals on both axes, displays deterioration as the sampling product approaches its critical value, and recovers the weighted L2 regularity needed for the estimate. This is useful for quantitative inverse-problem stability; no optimality or endpoint result is claimed.
